chapter: Lincoln Park and the name Kid
title: Replacing band members: Foster Lewis, Jake White and Eddie Garland
summary: Ory lost a Laplace player and found bass player Garland through Manuel Perez.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you still keep the same musicians that you'd brought from Laplace, or were you changing your band?
No, I had all the same music. Same musicians. And finally... Well, you lost one of them.
He got married and had to go back home. His bride wanted to go back, and that's when you got Tutti Garland.
Oh, Foster Lewis, yeah. Yeah. No, but he never did go. He never had come to New Orleans.
No, the one that came to New Orleans that got married, and his bride wanted to go back to Laplace, and you replaced him with Garland. Which one was it? Must have been a bass player.
He didn't come to New Orleans with you. No, that's Foster Lewis didn't. No.
Well, who was the one that took Foster Lewis's place? A guy named Jake White.
I just told you, he was the best player that I've ever heard in my life.

The world's greatest worst. Really? The world's greatest worst? Yeah. The world's greatest worst? Yeah. The world's greatest worst? Worth. Then Manuel Perez told me about Eddie Garland. He was playing at the Dixon Park two bands. Oh, yeah. And I told him I hadn't even known of a good bass player. He said, yeah, I know a guy driving the barrel wagon, Eddie Garland. He used to phone them. He used to phone them, I called. He was driving a what? A barrel wagon, the whole empty barrel of wine and whiskey. Oh, is that so?
